world.name: Veil
world.tagline: Yellow clouds hide a surface hotter than an oven.

objectives.text: Gases like carbon dioxide trap heat; too much makes a world far hotter.
objectives.chapter: CBSE Class 8 Science: Pollution of Air and Water

objectives.text: Liquid water needs a world at the right distance from its star: the habitable zone.
Air pushes back on fast-moving objects; spacecraft can use it to slow down.
The most fuel-efficient way between two orbits uses two well-timed burns.

flightLevels.title: Skim the Haze
flightLevels.brief: You're coming in way too fast to stop with fuel. Dip into Veil's thick air to slow down, but not too deep!
hints: Aim your path so it grazes the glowing haze, not the planet.
Too much heat? Your path is too deep. Nudge it outward a little.

flightLevels.title: Two-Burn Transfer
flightLevels.brief: Climb from a low orbit up to the Orrin relay ring using as little fuel as possible.
hints: Burn FORWARD (the way you're moving). That raises the far side of your orbit.
Coast to the highest point, then burn forward again to round out the orbit.

clues.title: CO₂ blanket
clues.data: Atmosphere 96% CO₂, about 90× thicker than Earth's, with sulfuric-acid clouds.
clues.dataCadet: The air is almost all carbon dioxide, a gas that traps heat. And it's super thick!

clues.title: Oven world
clues.data: Surface 460 °C, almost the same day and night, pole to equator. Heat is trapped everywhere.
clues.dataCadet: It's 460 °C everywhere, day AND night. The heat can't escape.

clues.title: Lost oceans
clues.data: Ripple marks and salt layers: this basin was a sea. The water is gone.
clues.dataCadet: Ripples and salt, so this was once a sea!

clues.title: Isotope clock
clues.data: Radioactive clock in the salt: the seas dried up slowly over ~1 billion years while starlight kept rising.
clues.dataCadet: A natural clock in the salt says the seas dried slowly while the starlight got stronger.

clues.title: Sleeping volcano
clues.data: Cold summit. The lava flows are hundreds of millions of years old.
clues.dataCadet: The volcano is cold and asleep, and has been for ages.

clues.title: Sulfur rock
clues.data: Rocks rich in sulfur: volcanoes were active long ago.
clues.dataCadet: Smelly sulfur rocks. Volcanoes were busy long ago.

clues.title: Few craters
clues.data: Very few craters. Old lava paved over the surface long ago.
clues.dataCadet: Hardly any craters. Old lava covered them up.

explanations.greenhouse: Thick CO₂ traps heat, the oceans boiled away, and the salt clock shows it happened as the starlight rose. A runaway greenhouse.
explanations.impact: There are hardly any craters, so no giant impact here.
explanations.stellar: Close! The star's rising light started it, but what's cooking Veil now is its thick heat-trapping air.
explanations.volcanism: Volcanoes added gas long ago, but they're cold now and can't explain heat that's still trapped today.
explanations.unknown: Honest answer. Mission Control will send data that helps.

glyph.prompt: Orrin bars: | = 1, ‖ = 2 … They count in twos (binary). What's next?

colony.note: Veil is closer to its star, but the thick clouds block much of the light.

questions.label: Is there a world like Veil near home?
questions.answer: Yes, Venus! 96% CO₂ and hotter than Mercury, even though it's farther from the Sun.

questions.label: Do stars get brighter as they age?
questions.answer: Yes. Sun-like stars slowly brighten. When our Sun was young it shone about 30% dimmer than it does today.

questions.label: Could oceans really boil away?
questions.answer: If a planet gets hot enough, water vapour rises high and is split apart by starlight. Then the hydrogen escapes to space.

questions.label: Can you send snacks?
questions.answer: Shipped! ETA: 76 years. Please share with Tobo.

report.unknownReveal: Your data shows thick CO₂, lost oceans and trapped heat: a runaway greenhouse, triggered by a brightening star.

signal.prompt: A new signal from deep space. What is it?

readings.label: Pulse period
readings.value: 0.033 s, precise as an atomic clock

readings.label: Source
readings.value: Tiny, super-dense object in a gas cloud

options.label: Pulsar (spinning dead star)
options.why: A super-precise, super-fast tick from a tiny dense object: a pulsar, the core left over from an exploded star.

options.label: Orrin probe
options.why: No message pattern this time. It's natural.

options.label: X-rays from gas falling into a black hole
options.why: That glow flickers; it doesn't tick perfectly.

options.label: Flare star
options.why: Flares don't repeat 30 times a second!

forge.goal: Tobo wants a calm, long-lasting star to recharge slowly.
forge.success: Slow and steady. Recharged. Hollow, here we come.

questions.speaker: kiran
questions.q: Veil is hotter than the planet closest to its star. Why?
options: Its thick CO₂ air traps heat
questions.misconception: Only distance from the star sets a planet's temperature.
questions.feedback: The air matters as much as the distance. In our Solar System, Venus is hotter than Mercury for the same reason.

questions.speaker: tobo
questions.q: "Greenhouse gases are always bad!" says Tobo. Hmm?
options: No. A little keeps a planet warm enough for life, too much overheats it
questions.feedback: Without any greenhouse effect, Earth would be frozen. It's all about balance.

questions.speaker: asha
questions.q: Why did skimming the haze slow us down?
options: Air pushes back on fast-moving things
questions.feedback: That push-back is drag. Real Mars orbiters used it to save fuel (aerobraking).

intro.t: Veil's surface is hot enough to melt lead.
Good news: no fuel needed to slow down! Bad news: we use the air instead.
Skim the haze. Not too deep.

afterFly.t: We're in! Scanners up. Those clouds look… suspicious.

correct.t: A runaway greenhouse. But it wasn't their factories. Their STAR got brighter.
The safe zone around the star moved outward… and left Veil behind.

wrong.t: We built for the wrong problem. The base starts low on supplies.

afterBuild.t: Survived the acid storm. My paint job did not.

afterReport.t: Another dip in the starlight. Another world. Let's go.

outro.t: Fragment 2: "OUR SKY GREW WARMER. THE LIGHT GREW STRONGER."
The light grew stronger… they're telling us about their star.
